hero.title: Building Sahelian communities resilient to climate change
hero.sub: We fight extreme poverty, hunger and the effects of climate change in northern Cameroon through food security, health, hygiene, child protection and reforestation.

about.title: A youth association that grew into a climate and poverty organisation
about.intro: Sahel Climate Action (SCA) is a non-profit organisation fighting extreme poverty, the effects of climate change and social inequality in the Sahel, with a focus on Cameroon. We run integrated programmes that help poor households become more resilient while protecting the environment. Communities, local authorities and technical partners shape every project with us.
about.vision: Resilient, inclusive and prosperous Sahelian communities where everyone can live with dignity, despite climate, economic and social challenges.
about.mission: To improve the lives of vulnerable people through social protection, food security, gender equality, agroforestry, ecosystem restoration and climate adaptation.
about.objectivesT: What we set out to do
objectives: Strengthen food security for vulnerable households.

history.text: Three-year strategic plan covering agriculture, food security, social protection, water, climate, gender, reforestation, waste and local economic development.
The association becomes Sahel Climate Action, a name that reflects the climate work it had carried out for years.
Registered as an association in Maroua.
Founded as the Association des Jeunes pour la Lutte contre la Pauvreté dans l’Extrême-Nord (AJELPEN).

how: Projects start from needs the communities express.
Beneficiaries take an active part and local skills are built up.
Results are tracked with clear indicators and reviewed every year.
Finances are open, and we answer to the people we serve and to our partners.
No one is left behind: women, young people, displaced people and people with disabilities are included.
about.leadersIntro: SCA is run by a General Assembly, a Board of Directors and an Executive Directorate, with regional branches and community committees.

programmes.title: What we do
programmes.intro: Five programmes run today. Pick one to see who it serves and what it has achieved.

items.title: Food security
items.line: Grain grown, stored and resold at cost.
items.body: Each year SCA grows maize, millet, sorghum, rice and groundnuts on farmland around Pakete, Pitoa and Wouro Labbo (Garoua) and Congola and Djarengol (Maroua). The harvest is stored, then sold at cost price, with no profit margin, during the June to September lean season when stocks run out and prices climb. Part of the proceeds funds our awareness and child-protection work. Women and young girls take part in production, storage and distribution.
facts: Production June to August, distribution June to September

items.title: Child protection
items.line: A hot meal and a listening ear for children living on the streets.
items.body: In Garoua and Maroua, children living on the streets receive hot, balanced meals made from local food, clean water and snacks. Meals open the door to hygiene sessions, health referrals, psychosocial support and, where possible, a return to family or school. Educational talks cover hygiene, child rights, drugs and violence, HIV and early pregnancy prevention, peaceful conflict resolution and life skills.
facts: 198 children in 2025: 125 in Maroua, 73 in Garoua

items.title: Health and awareness
items.line: Prevention campaigns that reach tens of thousands of people.
items.body: Through community sessions, radio shows, posters, door-to-door visits and voluntary screening, SCA spreads prevention messages across the North and Far North regions. Forty community relays were trained in 2023 in social-change communication, family hygiene and health-risk monitoring.
facts: 2025: 35,265 people on diabetes, cancer, heart disease and environmental illness
2025: 21,646 young people and adults on tobacco and drugs
2023: 38,125 girls and young women on early pregnancy and HIV/AIDS

items.title: Water, hygiene and sanitation
items.line: Clean hands, safe water, fewer disease outbreaks.
items.body: In 2023 SCA held hygiene sessions in low-income districts of Garoua and Maroua on handwashing, soap use, water treatment, waste management, latrine upkeep and cholera prevention. Building latrines and rehabilitating water points are planned next.
facts: 44,054 people reached: 21,664 in Garoua, 22,390 in Maroua

items.title: Climate action
items.line: Practical ways for farming families to cope with drought and floods.
items.body: Our campaigns teach water and soil conservation, climate-smart farming, drought-resistant seeds, agroforestry and community tree planting, land recovery, and early warning of climate risks. They also encourage everyday actions: planting trees, managing waste, saving water and energy, and fewer bush fires.

coming.title: Sustainable agriculture
coming.text: Farmer training, drought-resistant seeds, market gardens, drip irrigation, compost and cooperatives.

coming.title: Reforestation
coming.text: Tree nurseries, planting, living hedges, community orchards and school awareness.

coming.title: Gender equity
coming.text: Women’s leadership and cooperatives, entrepreneurship training, access to credit.

coming.title: Waste management
coming.text: Sorting, composting, recycling, clean-up campaigns and small recycling businesses.

coming.title: Local economic development
coming.text: Vocational training, microfinance, rural businesses and youth entrepreneurship.

coming.title: Wider social protection
coming.text: School kits, sponsorship of vulnerable children and support for isolated elderly people.

impact.title: Results we can show
impact.intro: Between 2023 and 2025 SCA gave food support to 13,270 households in two years and ran awareness campaigns that reached more than 180,000 people.
rows: People reached on hygiene and water
impact.chartNote: Counted per campaign, so some people are counted more than once.
value: Awareness campaign 2025: about 174 FCFA per person reached.
Street-children meals 2024: 63.7% of the budget buys food.

quotes.text: Thanks to this food aid, my family got through the hard season without going hungry.
The hygiene sessions taught us to protect our children better against disease.

lessons: Community involvement and close follow-up make the difference.
Trained community relays carry the message further.
Food aid works best together with health and hygiene awareness.
Respecting local culture and a gender-aware approach improve uptake.
impact.challenges: Logistics and rising transport costs, hard-to-reach neighbourhoods, tight budgets, bad weather and low buy-in from some households. We answer with stronger coordination with local authorities, volunteers, better delivery calendars and better monitoring.

where.title: Where we work
where.intro: We work in the cities of Garoua and Maroua and the villages and districts around them. Most households farm maize, millet, sorghum and groundnuts. Their main needs are food, safe water, health care, schooling and jobs.
where.farm: Pakete, Pitoa and Wouro Labbo near Garoua. Congola and Djarengol near Maroua.

partners.title: Partners
partners.intro: We work hand in hand with the people and institutions closest to the problem. Local authorities open doors, community organisations carry the work, and technical and financial partners help us grow.
